significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: the “Mechanism-Universality Score = fraction of the concept's variance that is cross-model reproducible” would separate scientific mechanisms from shortcuts and predict OOD retention, stitching transfer, and causal relevance. This would establish both a broad representational phenomenon and a consequential, though indirect, mechanism-validation principle, constraining how cross-model agreement should relate to several independently measurable outcomes; this is weightier than merely finding a concept direction, and it bears directly on the use of representational convergence as a generality benchmark exemplified by Edamadaka et al.’s 2025 matter-representation work and by CKA-based comparison methods such as Kornblith et al. (ICML 2019). The true and false states are distinguishable, and a negative result would importantly reject universality as a general validator, although the bundled hypothesis could leave ambiguity about whether failure arose from shared artifacts, architecture dependence, or the absence of the proposed relationship. Topic substitution fails: the generic topic would only ask whether scientific concepts correspond to mechanisms, whereas this claim specifically posits a cross-model universality-to-validity-and-generalization law, so the score is not inherited from the topic.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “Mechanism-Universality Score,” proposed as an “annotation-free audit” and predictor of whether an interpreted concept will survive OOD shifts, giving it ex-ante lead time when used to screen a concept before relying on or deploying the associated model behavior. After alignment and re-extraction in a new model, the claimed conclusion predicts a recurring relation—higher shared-subspace variance should imply greater OOD retention, transfer, and causal relevance—rather than merely supplying a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction. The asserted scope spans “protein,” “molecular,” and “materials models” with independently trained architectures, and the downstream users include scientific-model interpretability researchers and practitioners auditing which recovered concepts are trustworthy, though no concrete deployment gate or direct outside-AI scientific decision rule is specified. Topic substitution fails because the reusable score and its cross-model predictive coupling disappear when the specific hypothesis is removed; its reach therefore comes from the claim rather than from scientific foundation models being broadly important.
